Odoo Purchase: Cancel MPR & Return to Draft

step-by-step guide showing as shown how the Cancel MPR button was created on the Purchase RFQ, how it runs a Server Action, how the buttons are shown/hidden by Request Status, and how native Odoo tracking records the status changes.

Module
Purchase / Request for Quotation
Workflow
Draft ↔ For Procurement Review → Approved
Cancel action
For Procurement Review → Draft

Steps

  1. 1Confirm statuses
  2. 2Add Cancel MPR button
  3. 3Create Server Action
  4. 4Paste final code
  5. 5Create Contextual Action
  6. 6Link button to action
  7. 7Cancel MPR visibility
  8. 8Submit button visibility
  9. 9Hide standard Cancel
  10. 10Track Request Status
  11. 11Test the workflow
  12. 12Final checklist
Important: Cancel MPR does not cancel the Odoo RFQ and does not delete any MPR. It only changes the custom Request Status from For Procurement Review back to Draft so Maintenance can correct the request.
Keep the workflow simple: there is no Resubmit button. After a cancellation, Maintenance uses the same Submit for Review & Approval button again.
1

Confirm the three Request Status values

Open a Purchase RFQ in Studio, click Request Status, then click Edit Values.

Keep as shown these values:

Draft→For Procurement Review→Approved
Technical name: x_studio_request_status.
2

Add the Cancel MPR button in Studio

  1. On the RFQ header, click Add a button.
  2. Label: Cancel MPR.
  3. Select Run a Server Action.
  4. Do not use Call a method.
The Server Action does not exist yet at this point, so leave the action selection until after Steps 3–5.
3

Create a standalone Server Action — not an Automation Rule

Use the same pattern as the existing Submit RFQ for Procurement Review button.

  1. Exit Studio.
  2. Go to Settings → Technical → Actions → Server Actions.
  3. Click New.
  4. Name: Cancel MPR.
  5. Model: Purchase Order.
  6. Type: Execute Code.
No Trigger is required. The Studio button runs the Server Action directly.
4

Paste the final Cancel MPR Server Action code

Replace the default comments in the Code box with the complete code below.

Cancel MPR — final Server Action code
if not record:
    raise UserError("No RFQ record was found.")

status_field = env['purchase.order']._fields.get('x_studio_request_status')

if not status_field:
    raise UserError("Request Status field was not found.")

draft_value = False

for key, label in status_field._description_selection(env):
    if label == 'Draft':
        draft_value = key
        break

if not draft_value:
    raise UserError("Request Status value 'Draft' was not found.")

record.write({
    'x_studio_request_status': draft_value
})
Why there is no message_post(): we removed the custom HTML chatter message so native Odoo field tracking can show a clean status-change entry instead.
5

Create the contextual action only if it is required

  1. Save the Server Action.
  2. Use Create Contextual Action only if you also want this Server Action available from the record Action menu. It is not required merely to run the Server Action from a Studio button. If you do not need an Action-menu entry, leave the Server Action saved without creating a contextual action.
  3. After it is created, the button changes to Remove Contextual Action.
6

Link Cancel MPR to the Server Action

  1. Return to the RFQ and open Studio.
  2. Click Add a button or reopen the Cancel MPR button.
  3. Label: Cancel MPR.
  4. Select Run a Server Action.
  5. Under Action to run, select Cancel MPR.
  6. Click Confirm.
7

Show Cancel MPR only during Procurement Review

Click Cancel MPR → Invisible → Conditional.

Set the invisible rule so the button is hidden when Request Status is blank, Draft or Approved. We configured it as Match any:

  • Request Status is not set, OR
  • Request Status is in Draft, Approved.
Important: In Studio, build the condition by selecting the Request Status values from the interface. If you use a technical expression, first confirm the stored selection keys in Settings → Technical → Database Structure → Fields → Request Status; labels such as “Draft” do not guarantee that the stored key is draft.
Generated Invisible condition
not x_studio_request_status or x_studio_request_status in ['draft', 'approved']
Request StatusCancel MPR
Blank / NewHidden
DraftHidden
For Procurement ReviewVisible
ApprovedHidden
8

Hide Submit for Review & Approval after submission

Click Submit for Review & Approval → Invisible → Conditional.

Hide it when Request Status is For Procurement Review or Approved.

Generated Invisible condition
x_studio_request_status in ['for_procurement_review', 'approved']
Request StatusSubmit for Review & Approval
Blank / DraftVisible
For Procurement ReviewHidden
ApprovedHidden
9

Hide Odoo's standard Cancel button permanently

The grey Odoo Cancel button runs the standard Purchase method button_cancel. That is not our Maintenance workflow.

  1. In Studio, click the grey standard Cancel button.
  2. On the left, tick the checkbox beside Invisible.
  3. Do not use a condition; set it to always invisible.
  4. Do not click Remove from View.
Outside Studio, Maintenance should no longer see Odoo's standard Cancel button.
10

Turn on native tracking for Request Status

This gives the same clean chatter style used in the other modules.

  1. Go to Settings → Technical → Database Structure → Fields.
  2. Search for x_studio_request_status.
  3. Open Request Status (Purchase Order).
  4. Set Enable Ordered Tracking from 0 to 1.
  5. Save.

Now Odoo automatically logs changes such as:

SubmitDraft → For Procurement Review (Request Status)
Cancel MPRFor Procurement Review → Draft (Request Status)
11

Test the complete workflow

  1. Create or open a test RFQ.
  2. In Draft, Maintenance completes the RFQ/MPR details.
  3. Click Submit for Review & Approval.
  4. Confirm Request Status becomes For Procurement Review.
  5. Confirm the Procurement review activities are created by the existing Submit action.
  6. Use Cancel MPR when Maintenance needs to correct the request.
  7. Confirm Request Status returns to Draft.
  8. Confirm the RFQ and MPR data remain intact.
  9. Edit the request and use the same Submit for Review & Approval button again.
Draft→Submit for Review & Approval→For Procurement Review→Cancel MPR→Draft
Approved is different: once Procurement changes Request Status to Approved, Maintenance should no longer be able to update the record. That locking step is a separate configuration phase.
12

Final checklist

  • Request Status has only Draft, For Procurement Review and Approved
  • Cancel MPR is a Studio button running a Server Action
  • Cancel MPR Server Action changes Request Status back to Draft only
  • No Automation Rule / Trigger is used for the Cancel MPR button
  • Contextual Action is created only if an Action-menu entry is required
  • Cancel MPR is hidden in blank/Draft/Approved
  • Submit button is hidden in For Procurement Review/Approved
  • Standard Odoo Cancel is always invisible
  • Request Status ordered tracking = 1
  • Chatter shows native old → new Request Status history
  • No separate Resubmit button exists
  • Same Submit button is reused after corrections
Finished workflow: Maintenance works in Draft, submits to Procurement Review, can use Cancel MPR to return to Draft for corrections, and uses the same Submit button again. Approved remains the final Maintenance lock point.
